Integrated programme performance case study

From programme data to decisions.

One end to end example of how I connect programme delivery, financial control, data modelling and clear reporting to support project decisions.

Annual programme budget: R3 millionTotal managed: R9 million over three yearsFocus: Business Intelligence

Illustrative case data. My programme management experience involved an annual budget of R3 million over three years, R9 million in total. The dashboard below is a separate synthetic R5 million scenario. Its category allocations, actuals, forecasts and decision note are illustrative, not programme results. No learner, school or transaction records are shown.

01 · Performance dashboard

Connect delivery and financial performance.

The dashboard separates approved budget, eligible actuals and forecast costs. The estimate at completion combines spend to date with the remaining delivery plan.

Decision support

Base plan: forecast remains within budget.

Check outstanding commitments and remaining activity volumes before treating the projected balance as available.

How to use this view: the top line tests affordability, the category table points to where to review costs, and the controls help compare delivery and price assumptions before changing scope or approving a reallocation.

02 · Data model

Give every record a clear relationship.

An illustrative relational design connects planned activity to participation, results and cost records, so reporting can be traced back to the operational detail.

Programmeprogramme_id · budget · dates
one programme has many activities
Activityactivity_id · programme_id · date
Learnerlearner_id · school_id · grade
many learners attend many activities
Participationlearner_id · activity_id · attendance
Activityactivity_id
one activity records many outcomes
Resultresult_id · activity_id · measure
Activityactivity_id
one activity can have many transactions
Cost recordtransaction_id · activity_id · category

The participation table resolves the many to many relationship between learners and activities. Stable IDs and clear record grain make it possible to link attendance and results without double counting.

03 · Decision report

Turn the forecast into an action.

The model supports a short management update that separates what the data shows from what the team should confirm next.

Illustrative management read out · synthetic figures

What the forecast suggests

In the base scenario, estimated final spend is R4.68 million against a R5 million budget, leaving R320,000 below budget.

  • Confirm that the remaining activity schedule matches the delivery volume used in this scenario.
  • Check open commitments and pending transactions before considering any budget reallocation.
  • At the next review, compare delivered activity and participation with the volumes used in the forecast.
Sample report excerpt · illustrative only
Forecast spend remains within the approved envelope. Before reallocating the projected balance, confirm the remaining operations schedule and outstanding commitments. Update the forecast after the next delivery review.

04 · Financial logic

Show the calculations behind the result.

The first three examples match the financial model workbook. The additional scenario formula shows how the controls scale remaining costs when delivery or unit cost assumptions change.

Recognized actuals by category=SUMIFS('Clean Actuals'!$M$6:$M$155,'Clean Actuals'!$D$6:$D$155,A7,'Clean Actuals'!$C$6:$C$155,"<="&'Assumptions'!$B$5)Adds eligible actual spend for one category up to the reporting cut off.
Estimate at completion=C7+E7Actuals to cut off plus forecast to complete.
Variance to budget=B7-F7Approved budget less estimate at completion.
Scenario forecast to completeFixed cost + (Variable cost × delivery volume × unit cost index)Tests how remaining activity and cost assumptions change the forecast, while leaving actuals and approved budget fixed.

The first three formulas are taken from the financial model workbook. The final formula describes the illustrative logic used by the interactive scenario.
